extracted.intended_audience: users of the Singular computer algebra system (mathematicians, researchers, and programmers)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for Singular functions and system variables: syntax, types, purpose, notes, and examples for each function in Chapter 5. Intended to guide correct use of the functions and interpret their outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: simplex output list L
rubrics_metrics.description: Layout of the list L returned by the simplex procedure: L[1]=matrix, L[2]=int (0=finitely many solution, 1=unbounded, -1=no solution, -2=error), L[3]=intvec mapping rows to variable numbers, L[4]=intvec mapping columns to non-basis variable numbers, L[5]=int (number of constraints m), L[6]=int (number of variables n). The solution can be read off the first column of L[1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes example showing how to interpret L entries and refers to simplexOut for formatted output. Illustrative numeric example provided; see Section D.8.3.8 [simplexOut].

rubrics_metrics.name: simplify
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the 'simplified' first argument (poly, vector, ideal, or module) according to simplification rules specified by an int expression argument (bitflags for different rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of bitflag rules: 1 normalize (divide by leading coefficient if a unit), 2 erase zero generators/columns, 4 erase copies of earlier generators/columns, 8 erase scalar multiples of earlier generators, 16 erase generators whose leading monomials are copies with unit coefficients, 32 erase generators whose leading terms are divisible by others, 64 normalize each coefficient of every monomial. Examples show behavior on ideals, matrices and modules (e.g., simplify(i,1), simplify(i,2), etc.). See Section 4.5 [ideal], 4.13 [module], 4.16 [poly], 4.21 [vector].

rubrics_metrics.name: size
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns an int depending on the type of the argument: for ideals/modules number of non-zero generators; for strings/intvec/list/resolution length; for poly/vector number of monomials; for matrix/intmat number of entries (rows*columns); for ring returns number of elements in ground field or -1; for number/bigint returns 0 for 0 or number of words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: size("hello")==5; size(poly) gives number of monomials; size(module) returns number of generators. See related functions ncols/nrows and type-specific sections referenced. See Section 4.5, 4.7, 4.8, 4.13, 4.16, 4.20, 4.21.

rubrics_metrics.name: slimgb
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a (slim) Groebner basis of an ideal or module with respect to the basering ordering; designed to keep polynomials short with small coefficients. A reduced Groebner basis is returned if option(redSB) is set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm aims to keep polynomials 'slim'; progress can be viewed with option(prot). Example provided. References to slim Groebner bases theory and links to option(redSB) and std. See Section A.2.3 and related commands (std, groebner).

rubrics_metrics.name: sortvec
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes an intvec permutation v which orders the ideal/module by its initial terms starting with the smallest, i.e., I(v[i]) < I(v[i+1]) for all i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: sortvec(I) returns a permutation ordering generators by initial terms. See general lib reference D.2.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: sqrfree
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes squarefree factors of a polynomial, returning factors (as an ideal) and optionally multiplicities (as an intvec) depending on second argument. Variants: with second arg 0,1,2,3 produce different outputs (factors+multiplicities, non-constant factors, non-constant factors+mult., squarefree part respectively).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not implemented for coefficient fields real and finite fields of type (p^n,a). Examples show different return forms: sqrfree(f), sqrfree(f,1), sqrfree(f,2), sqrfree(f,3). See factorize for related functionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: sprintf
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting function sprintf(fmt, ...) that returns a string formed according to a format control string fmt and additional arguments; supports conversion specifications and some additions (%n and %2 produce newline without consuming an argument).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an additional argument is a list, wrap it in list() to avoid flattening. Many format specifiers supported; see help print. Examples demonstrate formatting of rings, modules, intmat, and using %p, %;, %b etc. See related print/fprintf/printf and string section.

rubrics_metrics.name: sres
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes a free resolution of an ideal or module using Schreyer’s method; input must be a standard basis. sres(M,k) stops after k steps; sres(M,0) returns list of n modules where n is number of base ring variables. Returns a resolution list L where L[1]=M, L[2] is standard basis of first syzygy module, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if not minimal, betti command gives true Betti numbers. Accessing elements may trigger partial computations. Examples show calling sres and printing betti. See related commands betti, fres, hres, lres, minres, mres, res, syz.

rubrics_metrics.name: status
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the status of a link when called as status(link, string). Allowed status queries include 'name','type','open','openread','openwrite','read','write','mode','exists'. If called with a third argument, returns int comparing status to given string. Also status(list, timeout) checks readiness of list of links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return semantics: -2 error, -1 all links closed/at eof, 0 timeout, >0 at least one ready; examples show status on links and use with open/read/write. See open/read/write and link section.

rubrics_metrics.name: std
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes a standard basis of an ideal or module with respect to the basering monomial ordering. Various optional signatures allow Hilbert-driven computation, addition of generators, and use of weights for quasihomogeneous ideals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation is a straightforward Buchberger/Mora algorithm; for global orderings use groebner which heuristically picks best algorithm. Use option(prot) to view progress. Examples: local computation, Hilbert-driven elimination, quasihomogeneous elimination using hilb result. See related commands facstd, fglm, groebner, mstd, option, stdfglm, stdhilb.

rubrics_metrics.name: stdfglm
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the standard basis of an ideal in the basering via fglm converting from an ordering given as second argument to the basering ordering (default 'dp'). If optional second arg is 'std' or 'slimgb', uses those instead of groebner to compute the starting basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show converting from dp to lp and using specified source ordering strings (including weighted orderings). See fglm, groebner, slimgb, std, stdhilb.

rubrics_metrics.name: stdhilb
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes a Groebner basis of an ideal/module by using the Hilbert-driven Groebner basis algorithm; optional arguments specify whether to use 'std' or 'slimgb' and variable weights (intvec w).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: homogenize with weights if not homogeneous, compute Groebner basis of homogenization, compute Hilbert function, then Groebner basis in original ring. If provided weights don't match basering variable weights, result may not be a Groebner basis in original ring. Examples compare outputs and show equivalence via hilb/std. See groebner, slimgb, std, stdfglm.

rubrics_metrics.name: subst
rubrics_metrics.description: Substitutes one or more ring/parameter variables by polynomial(s) in a poly, vector, ideal, or module. Multiple substitution pairs are performed sequentially (not simultaneously). Coefficients must be polynomial when substituting a parameter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate sequential substitution order: subst(f,x,y,y,z) first substitutes x->y then y->z. See map, module, poly, vector, and substitute library reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: system
rubrics_metrics.description: Interface to internal data and the operating system. system(string [, expression]) performs a variety of commands determined by the first string argument; return type depends on command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long list of supported commands documented (e.g., 'alarm', 'absFact', 'browsers', 'bracket', 'cpu', 'denom_list', 'eigenvals', 'env', 'executable', 'freegb', 'getenv', 'getPrecDigits', 'HC', 'hessenberg', 'install', 'LLL', 'nblocks', 'nc_hilb', 'neworder', 'newstruct', 'opp', 'oppose', 'pid', 'random', 'reduce_bound', 'reserve', 'reservedLink', 'semaphore', 'setenv', 'sh', 'shrinktest', 'Singular', 'SingularLib', 'spadd', 'spectrum', 'stest', 'tensorModuleMult', 'twostd', 'uname', 'version', 'with', '--' long options). Notes: not all functions work on every platform; examples show shell commands and option setting (e.g., system('--min-time','0.02')). See related command docs.

rubrics_metrics.name: syz
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the first syzygy module (module of relations of the given generators) of an ideal or module. Optional second argument selects the Groebner base algorithm: 'std' (default) or 'slimgb'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If option(returnSB) is set and using 'std', a standard basis is returned; otherwise a generating set. Example: syz(x,y) returns [y,-x]. See fres, hres, lift, lres, mres, nres, res, option, std.

rubrics_metrics.name: trace
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the trace of an intmat as an int, or of a matrix as a poly (sum of diagonal entries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: intmat m[2][2]=1,2,3,4; trace(m) -> 5. See matrix and intmat sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: transpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Transposes an intmat, matrix, or module; return type corresponds to argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: transpose(matrix[2][3]) swaps rows and columns. See matrix/intmat/module sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: type
rubrics_metrics.description: Prints the name, level, type and value of a variable when used as 'type name;' or 'type(name);'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To display the value of an expression, it's sufficient to type the expression followed by ';'. Examples: i; shows value, type(i); prints comment like '// i int 3'. See data types and listvar/print.

rubrics_metrics.name: typeof
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the type of an expression as a string. For expression lists returns type of first element. Possible return types include 'ideal','int','intmat','intvec','list','map','matrix','module','number','none','poly','proc','qring','resolution','ring','string','vector' (internal '?unknown type?' exists).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show typeof on numbers, previously printed values, and that typeof(_) may return '?unknown type?' for certain internal cases. See data types.

rubrics_metrics.name: univariate
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns 0 if not univariate, -1 for a constant, or the variable number of the univariate polynomial (i.e., which variable it's univariate in).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: univariate(x^2+1) -> 1; univariate(x^2+y+1) -> 0; univariate(1) -> -1; var(univariate(z)) -> z. See leadexp and var functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: uressolve
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes all complex roots of a zero-dimensional ideal using either the multipolynomial Macaulay resultant (arg=1, only for homogeneous ideals) or the sparse resultant (arg=0) of Gelfand-Kapranov-Zelevinsky. Returns list; third arg defines precision for rationals; fourth arg (0,1,2) gives number of extra Laguerre runs for improved results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sparse resultant uses mixed polyhedral subdivision and resultant matrices; u-resultant and Laguerre’s algorithm find roots. If ground field is complex, list elements are numbers; otherwise strings. See laguerre and mpresmat for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: vandermonde
rubrics_metrics.description: vandermonde(p,v,d) computes the unique polynomial of degree d with prescribed values v[1],...,v[N] at given points p0,...,p_{N-1}, where N=(d+1)^n (n = number of ring variables). The returned polynomial is the solution of the transposed Vandermonde linear system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns a polynomial expressed as sum of monomials c_{α1...αn} x^{α1}...x^{αn} with α1+...+αn ≤ d. Example and construction notes sketched; see related theory and implementation details.
